related_questions.question: What is the difference between a hemorrhagic stroke and an ischemic CT scan?
related_questions.snippet: A CT scan can be used to show if there is bleeding in the affected area of the brain. The absence of bleeding on the scan suggests the stroke is ischemic or caused by a blood clot. By comparison, a hemorrhagic stroke will reveal bleeding in the CT scan.
related_questions.title: Ischemic vs Hemorrhagic Strokes: Types & Symptoms - Aviv Clinics

related_questions.question: How long does it take for an ischemic stroke to show on CT?

text_blocks.snippet: Ischemic stroke changes may not be visible on CT scans for several hours after the event. While some early signs like the hyperdense MCA sign can be seen within the first few hours, significant changes in brain tissue density (hypodensity) may take 12-24 hours to appear.

list.title: Early signs (within a few hours):
list.snippet: In some cases, early signs like the hyperdense MCA sign (a bright spot in the middle cerebral artery indicating a clot) or a dense vessel sign can be seen relatively quickly.

list.title: Later changes (12-24 hours):
list.snippet: More noticeable changes, such as a decrease in tissue density (hypodensity) in the affected area, typically become visible within 12-24 hours.

list.title: Normal CT:
list.snippet: In the initial hours after an ischemic stroke, a CT scan may appear normal even if brain tissue is damaged.

list.title: CT perfusion:
list.snippet: CT perfusion scans, which assess blood flow, can help identify the ischemic penumbra (tissue at risk) earlier than a standard CT.

list.title: MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI):
list.snippet: MRI, particularly DWI, is more sensitive than CT for detecting early ischemic changes and can show abnormalities within minutes of stroke onset.
